name: Profhilo Structura
lead: Profhilo Structura is an injectable hyaluronic acid (HA) product made by IBSA Farmaceutici, marketed as a medical device for restoring facial volume and contour, particularly in superficial fat compartments of the face such as the lateral cheek. It is a variant of the original Profhilo "skin remodelling" product and uses the same patented NAHYCO hybrid technology, which combines high- and low-molecular-weight HA into thermally stabilised complexes without chemical cross-linking.[1][2]

In a published case series, the product delivered 45 mg each of high-molecular-weight (about 1400 kDa) and low-molecular-weight (about 100 kDa) HA in a 2 mL syringe, and was placed with a cannula into the superficial fat compartment of each hemiface.[1] Its manufacturer-linked and independent clinicians describe it as a way to address the loss of facial fat volume associated with ageing, rather than as a conventional bolus filler.

Published evidence is limited to a small case series, an observational pilot study, laboratory comparisons with other HA fillers and a registered ongoing trial. These report improvements in clinician- and patient-rated measures, but they are small, uncontrolled and, in several cases, linked to the manufacturer.[1][2][3][4]

paras: Profhilo Structura is presented by its developers as a hybrid HA product with a much higher HA content than the original Profhilo. In the NAHYCO process, high- and low-molecular-weight HA chains are heated to form cooperative complexes; laboratory work comparing Profhilo, Profhilo Structura, a linear HA and cross-linked fillers examined how these products perform and how reversible they are with hyaluronidase.[1][2]

Unlike products designed mainly to add bulk, Profhilo Structura is described in the published literature as aiming to restore adipose tissue homeostasis, with HA proposed to influence adipocytes and surrounding tissue.[1] This mechanism is a hypothesis stated by the authors rather than an established finding.

A 2024 practical review in Plastic and Aesthetic Nursing, supported by the manufacturer, reports that the 45 mg total HA content and the rheological properties of the product were formulated to restore facial adipose tissue. Its authors, three invited experts, propose that the superficial medial and lateral-temporal cheek fat compartments are good candidates because they are involved early in facial ageing, and describe techniques developed for patients with early hypotrophy of the preauricular area (so-called sinkers).[5]

In the laboratory comparison, implants of the 45 mg/mL hybrid complex remained detectable by ultrasound in an animal model for 29 weeks, versus 4 weeks for a linear HA, 10 weeks for the 32 mg/mL hybrid complex (Profhilo) and at least 33 weeks for a cross-linked HA; enzymatic degradation studies were used to assess reversibility.[2]

The entry is discussed in the context of non-surgical face contouring, particularly "sunken" or flattened cheeks and mid-face support. Practitioners and patients describe it as a lower-bulk alternative to larger-volume fillers.[1][3] No community material on it is cited here.

The manufacturer-linked literature describes the hybrid cooperative complexes as pseudoplastic, flowing easily through a syringe and cannula, with lower viscosity than cross-linked HA fillers.[1] Authors propose that the product acts on adipose tissue and the surrounding matrix to support fat compartments, while noting this as a working hypothesis.[1][6]

A case series in the journal Gels followed 22 volunteers aged 36 to 60 years who received 2 mL of Profhilo Structura per hemiface via a 25-gauge cannula into the superficial fat compartment, and reported efficacy for adipose tissue restoration in the face.[1]

An observational pilot study published in 2024 examined the efficacy and tolerability of the product in the lateral cheek fat compartment.[3] A 2022 laboratory and in vivo comparison of four HA products, including Profhilo and Profhilo Structura, studied their performance and reversibility.[2]

In the 2024 pilot study, 50 healthy subjects received two injections one month apart and were evaluated three months later using investigator scales (the Facial Volume Loss Scale and the Wrinkle Severity Rating Scale) and their own self-assessments.[3] In the 2023 case series, soft-tissue thickness increased immediately after injection, improvement persisted across six months of follow-up, and participants reported satisfaction with the midface with no adverse effects.[1]

A 2026 study in 15 mice injected the product twice and examined dermal white adipose tissue after two months, reporting a different distribution of adipocyte sizes in treated animals than in controls, with more very large adipocytes.[6]

A trial registered as NCT06719154 and titled as an evaluation of the safety and efficacy of Profhilo Structura began recruiting in September 2024 with a planned enrolment of 164 people with skin ageing.[4] Results have not been published. No large independent randomised trials have been published.

As with other injectable HA products, procedures carry risks that clinicians describe, including bruising, swelling and injection-site reactions. Safety reporting specific to Profhilo Structura is limited to small studies. Post-marketing surveillance of the broader Profhilo hybrid HA family has been published separately.[1][3]

card.summary: A high-concentration hybrid hyaluronic acid injectable aimed at restoring cheek and facial fat volume, backed so far by small case series.
card.note: Evidence is small studies; large registered trial has no published results yet.

quick.overview:
Profhilo Structura is a hybrid hyaluronic acid product from IBSA that is injected by a clinician into superficial facial fat layers, mainly the cheeks, to restore volume and contour.
Published data so far consist of a 22-person case series, an observational pilot study and lab comparisons, with a 164-person trial still registered as ongoing.
quick.mechanism: It combines high- and low-molecular-weight hyaluronic acid into stable complexes using the NAHYCO process, without chemical cross-linking. Authors propose it may influence fat tissue homeostasis, though this is a hypothesis.
quick.risks: Risks described for injectable HA generally include bruising, swelling and injection-site reactions. Product-specific safety data are limited to small studies, and it is administered only by trained clinicians.

chain: Hybrid HA placed in superficial cheek fat compartments
Fuller, less hollow cheeks and smoother contour
angle.text: Profhilo Structura is used to restore volume in flattened or hollow cheeks and the preauricular area. Clinicians describe it as aiming at the superficial fat layer rather than adding a bolus of filler, giving a softer contour.
